chunks: Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn ibn Abi Al-Khattab narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Musa narrated to me, saying:

When my uncle Muhammad ibn Ja'far revolted in Mecca and invited the people to himself, he was called the Commander of the Faithful and allegiance was pledged to him for the Caliphate. Ar-Ridha (peace be upon him) and I entered upon him, and he said to him: 'O uncle! Do not contradict your father and your brother, for this matter will not be completed.'

Then he departed, and I departed with him to Medina. He did not stay long until Al-Jaludi arrived, met him, and defeated him. Then he asked for immunity from him, wore black, ascended the pulpit, and dethroned himself, saying: 'This matter belongs to Al-Ma'mun, and I have no right to it.'
Then he was sent to Khorasan, and he died in Jurjan.

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Ar-Ridha, title of Imam Ali ibn Musa
key_terms.السَّوَاد: Black garment, symbol of Abbasid rule
key_terms.الْجَلُودِيُّ: Al-Jaludi, Abbasian general who defeated Muhammad ibn Ja'far
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ: Muhammad ibn Ja'far, known as Al-Da'iy ila'l-Haqq, uncle of Imam Ar-Ridha

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ar-Ridha say to his uncle Muhammad ibn Ja'far when he claimed the Caliphate?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the pivotal moment when Imam Ali al-Rida (a.s.) visited his uncle, Muhammad ibn Ja'far (Al-Da'iy ila'l-Haqq), during his political uprising in Mecca. The Imam’s counsel that 'this matter will not be perfected' underscores the Shia distinction between political revolt and divinely appointed Imamate, a theme reinforced by the uncle’s subsequent abdication to Caliph Al-Ma'mun and death in exile.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 47-8 Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq narrated that Sa’d ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Muhammad ibn Al-Husayn Abil Khattab, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Musa,

“When my uncle Muhammad ibn Ja’far revolted in Mecca and invited the people towards himself, he was called the Commander of the Faithful and the people had pledged allegiance to him. Ar-Ridha’ (a.s.) and I went to see him and told him, ‘O uncle! Do not refute your father and brother. This rule of yours will not last.’

The Imam (a.s.) said this and departed along with me for Medina. A short time later Al-Joloodi went there, fought with and defeated him. He asked for immunity, wore a black garment, climbed up the pulpit and dethroned himself saying, ‘This rule is that of Al-Ma’mun. I have no rights to it.’
He then left there to go to Khorasan, but died in Gorgan (north of Iran).”
